main:
IN MEMORIAM
[ PHOTO: IN MEMORIAM ]

In memory of the four unarmed Trisakti University students shot dead with live ammunition inside their own campus gates on May 12, 1998: Elang Mulia Lesmana, Hery Hertanto, Hafidin Royan, and Hendriawan Sie.

In memory of the more than 1,190 human beings burned alive, shot, or beaten to death across Jakarta, Surakarta, Medan, and Palembang over three days in May 1998—hundreds of whom, including urban poor and children, were trapped and incinerated inside shopping malls such as Yogya Plaza Klender after the exits were locked and doused with fuel.

In recognition of the hundreds of ethnic Chinese-Indonesian women and girls—at least 85 to nearly 400 documented by the Tim Relawan untuk Kemanusiaan and the Joint Fact-Finding Team (TGPF)—who were systematically hunted down in their homes, shops, and streets across Glodok, Pluit, Jembatan Lima, and Tanah Abang, gang-raped in front of their families, sexually mutilated with razor blades and broken glass, and thrown into burning buildings. And in memory of Ita Martadinata Haryono (18), a Chinese-Indonesian high school student, survivor, and volunteer counselor who was brutally stabbed to death and had her throat slit in her Jakarta bedroom on October 9, 1998—just days before she was scheduled to fly to New York to testify before the United Nations about the May 1998 gang rapes. Not a single organizer, commander, or perpetrator was ever convicted.

In memory of labor organizer Marsinah (24), abducted, raped, tortured, and murdered in East Java in May 1993; journalist Fuad Muhammad Syafruddin ('Udin') of Harian Bernas, beaten to death in Yogyakarta in August 1996; and the 13 pro-democracy activists abducted in 1997–1998 who were forcibly disappeared and never returned to their families: poet Wiji Thukul, Bimo Petrus Anugerah, Herman Hendrawan, Suyat, Yani Afri, Sonny, Dedi Hamdun, Noval Alkatiri, Ismail, Ucok Munandar Siahaan, Hendra Hambali, Yadin Muhidin, and Abdun Nasser.

In memory of the 18 students, schoolchildren, and citizens killed when security forces fired live rounds into crowds protesting the 1998 MPR Special Session along Jalan Sudirman and the Atma Jaya campus: Bernardinus Realino Norma Irmawan ('Wawan') (20, Atma Jaya student shot in the chest while carrying a wounded classmate), Teddy Wardhani Kusuma (ITI), Sigit Prasetyo (YAI), Heru Sudibyo, Engkus Kusnadi (Universitas Jakarta), Muzammil Joko (Universitas Indonesia), high school student Lukman Firdaus, 6-year-old Ayu Ratna Sari (killed by a stray bullet to the head), Uga Usmana, Abdullah / Donit, Agus Setiana, Budiono, Doni Effendi, Rinanto, Sidik, Kristian Nikijulong, and Hadi.

In memory of the students and citizens shot dead in Jakarta, Lampung, and Palembang while protesting the State of Danger Bill (RUU PKB) on the eve of the 1999 MPR General Session: Yap Yun Hap (21, Universitas Indonesia electrical engineering student shot dead at Semanggi), Zainal Abidin, Teja Sukmana, M. Nuh Ichsan, Salim Jumadoi, Fadly, Deny Julian, Yusuf Rizal, Saidatul Fitria (Universitas Lampung), and Meyer Ardiansyah (IBA Palembang).

In memory of the thousands of civilians tortured, raped, and executed during the decade of Daerah Operasi Militer (DOM) in Aceh, the 46 civilians gunned down at the Simpang KKA Massacre in North Aceh (May 3, 1999), and the 57 villagers—including Teungku Bantaqiah and his students—massacred and dumped into mass graves in Beutong Ateuh (July 23, 1999). In memory of the more than 1,400 East Timorese civilians slaughtered by military-backed militias in 1999 at the Liquiça Church, the home of Manuel Carrascalão, the Suai Church, Maliana, and Dili, alongside murdered journalists Agus Muliawan and Sander Thoenes. And in memory of the thousands of civilians killed and displaced in the communal violence in Ambon/Maluku and Sambas, West Kalimantan.

We Refuse to Forget.

images: Majalah TEMPO & Pusat Data dan Analisa Tempo (PDAT): Archival photojournalism of the May 1998 riots, the Trisakti and Semanggi student protests, B.J. Habibie's cabinet, the June 1999 legislative elections, and the October 1999 MPR General Session.
LKBN Antara (Antara Foto): Official state wire photographs of Merdeka Palace, Bina Graha, the DPR/MPR Senayan complex, and regional visits.
Harian Kompas, Majalah Gatra, Forum Keadilan, Republika & The Jakarta Post: Contemporary 1998–1999 Indonesian press photography and editorial archives.

International Wire Services (Associated Press / AP, Reuters & Agence France-Presse / AFP): Press photographs covering the Asian Financial Crisis, IMF negotiations, the 1999 East Timor UNAMET ballot, and Jakarta street demonstrations.
Arsip Nasional Republik Indonesia (ANRI), Perpustakaan Nasional RI & Wikimedia Commons: Public domain state portraits, parliamentary emblems, and party insignia.

Archival & Fair Use Notice: Historical photographs and press images used in this project were gathered via public Google Search from online press archives and historical repositories. All photographs remain the property of their respective photojournalists and media publications (including TEMPO, Kompas, Antara, and international wire agencies) and are presented here solely for non-commercial, educational, and historical documentation purposes.
